Print and plot everything about any object of the package: its summary, its checks and every plot

Source: R/wildcards.R
overview.Rd

overview() prints and plots everything about any object the package returns: the summary, the diagnostic checks where the object has them, and every plot the object can draw. What is shown depends on the object:

  • a profile, class or transition fit of lpa(), lca(), multilpa(), multilca() or lta() (class multilpa_transitions): the output of report(), that is, the summary, the descriptives, the checks and every plot view;

  • a fit of another family (a mixture regression, a growth mixture, a general transition fit, an additive or a cross-level fit): its summary, the checks of diagnostics(), and the plots of plot_all();

  • pooled imputations: the summary and the plots of plot_all();

  • an enumeration grid: its summary and the plots of plot_all() (criteria, entropy, AvePP, criterion changes, heat map, smallest class, trust and tree);

  • a comparison, a bootstrap test, a bootstrap table of parameter_inference() or a sensitivity analysis: the object or its summary printed, and its plot;

  • a diagnostics() result: the result printed, and the plots of the fit it checked.

Usage

overview(x, plots = TRUE)

Arguments

x

Any object returned by the package: a fitted model, pooled imputations, an enumeration grid, a comparison, a bootstrap result, a sensitivity analysis or a diagnostics result.

plots

Whether to draw the plots:

  • TRUE (default): prints, then draws every plot. The plots need the ggplot2 package; without it only the printed part is shown;

  • FALSE: prints only.

Value

x, invisibly. The function is called for what it prints and draws.

Errors: latents_not_a_fit when x is not a fit, grid or other result of the package, for example a data frame; latents_bad_argument when plots is not TRUE or FALSE.

See also

report() for the fits it covers; plot_all() for the plots alone; get_checks() for the checks as a table.

Examples

fit <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,
                          n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
overview(fit, plots = FALSE)
#> Model fit
